Derivatives of smooth functions

Source: R/smooth_diagnostics.R
smooth_derivatives.Rd

The first derivative \(df/dx\) of each one-variable smooth, with pointwise and simultaneous confidence bands: where the band excludes 0, the smooth is increasing (or decreasing).

Usage

smooth_derivatives(
  object,
  term = NULL,
  n = 100,
  level = 0.95,
  nsim = 10000,
  seed = NULL,
  h = NULL
)

Arguments

object

a fitted model with smooth terms.

term

optional term labels (as in summary(), e.g. "s(lnaadt)"); by default every smooth.

n

number of grid points for one-variable smooths (the grid of a two-variable smooth has round(sqrt(n) * 3) points per variable).

level

confidence level of the bands.

nsim

number of draws for the simultaneous bands.

seed

optional seed for those draws (the caller's random-number stream is left unchanged).

h

step for the central differences of the basis (default 1e-4 times the range of the variable).

Value

A data frame like that of smooth_estimates(), with the derivative in fit.

Details

The derivative is exact for the linear predictor up to the central-difference error of the basis: with \(D = (X(x + h) - X(x - h)) / 2h\), \(df/dx = D b\) and its standard error is \(\sqrt{D V D'}\). Simultaneous bands are computed as in smooth_estimates().

See also

plot_derivatives()
